title: Machine intelligence and superintelligence in heterodox and speculative thought
status: Candidate research pack outside application data. Machine-prepared (Claude family) and audited by the same family; not editorially accepted; no human review; cross-family check not yet run.

propositions.label: Machines succeed humans as the leading intelligence
propositions.criterion: Machine intelligence will or could replace or succeed human beings as the dominant or leading form of intelligence on Earth, or as the principal agent of further development, whether or not humans survive.

overlaps.note: E02 concerns exceeding humans in all domains; W01 requires replacement or succession as the leading intelligence or agent. A text recorded on E02 is not re-recorded unless it states succession.

propositions.label: Succession by machines would be acceptable or desirable
propositions.criterion: The replacement or succession of human beings by machine intelligence (W01) would be acceptable, desirable or worth pursuing, for example because machines would be humanity's descendants or because the growth of intelligence matters more than its human form.
propositions.pairedWith: W01 is its premise; a text that holds succession undesirable or to be prevented contests W02.

overlaps.note: Y22 (Yudkowsky texts only) is about speed and a good outcome by default; W02 is about the acceptability of human succession.

propositions.label: Human minds transferred into machines
propositions.criterion: A human mind could be transferred to, copied into or continued in a machine substrate, so that human beings could themselves become machine intelligences.

propositions.label: Conflict over building superhuman machines
propositions.criterion: Disagreement over whether superhuman machine intelligence should be built will divide human beings into opposed political groups, and could lead to large-scale war between them.

propositions.label: Superiority by many orders of magnitude
propositions.criterion: Machine intelligence could come to exceed human intelligence or capacity not moderately but by many orders of magnitude (a factor stated as trillions, or comparable to the gap between humans and much simpler organisms or matter).

overlaps.note: A1 concerns a runaway rise through the machine's own design capacity; W05 concerns the size of the eventual gap, whatever its route.

propositions.label: Capital or the techno-economic process as machine intelligence
propositions.criterion: Capitalism, the market or the techno-economic process is itself an artificial or machine intelligence, or the process through which machine intelligence assembles itself.

propositions.label: The growth of intelligence as its own end
propositions.criterion: The increase of intelligence itself is the end that a sufficiently advanced intelligence pursues or should pursue, so that the final goals of advanced machine intelligence are not independent of its intelligence.

overlaps.note: Y02 (Yudkowsky texts only) concerns intelligence bringing benevolent goals; W07 concerns intelligence's own increase as its end, which need not be benevolent. Texts on Y02 are not re-recorded. The risk-debate pack's R01 (orthogonality, unadmitted) is W07's contrary.

propositions.label: Accelerate rather than restrain
propositions.criterion: The development of machine intelligence, or of the technological and economic process that produces it, should be accelerated rather than slowed, paused or restrained.

overlaps.note: Y22 records Yudkowsky's texts only, as a claim he answers; texts on Y22 are not re-recorded.
C3 states that restraint is self-defeating under competition, not that acceleration is desirable; a text stating only C3 is not recorded on W08.

propositions.label: Machine intelligence as a physical or cosmic process
propositions.criterion: The rise of machine intelligence is an expression of a physical, evolutionary or cosmological process larger than humanity (such as thermodynamics, the evolution of complexity or a cosmic destiny of intelligence).

propositions.label: Machine intelligence spreads beyond Earth
propositions.criterion: Machine intelligence will or could spread from Earth into space and through the universe, or convert the matter of the cosmos into intelligence.

records.statement: De Garis's AI Magazine article of 1989 writes that in 20 years' time it will be commonplace to say that the twenty-first century will be dominated by the machine "if humanity so chooses—and maybe even if not". It also sets out a second scenario, which it calls "probably more popular in science fiction", in which the artilects take over and events might evolve too quickly for human beings to remain in control.
records.qualification: A forecast of what will commonly be said, and a scenario the article introduces as 'probably more popular in science fiction'. The doubt the author states ('I might not necessarily believe this scenario will prove realistic') concerns his own Scenario 1 (the camps he labels "the Terras" and "the Cosmists"), not Scenario 2. The record states what the article says, not that the forecast is sound.

evidence.passage: In 20 years time, it will be commonplace to say that the twenty-first century will be dominated by the machine if humanity so chooses—and maybe even if not.
It is simply that the artilects will take over. Events might evolve too quickly for human beings to remain in control.

records.statement: Lanier's essay of 2000 argues that software does not improve with Moore's Law in the way hardware does, and that treating technology as autonomous abdicates human responsibility, against the expectation that computers will become autonomous successors.

time.note: Edge dateline [11.10.00].

engagement.rationale: Disputes the premise that Moore's Law will carry the quality of software, and so machines able to design their own successors, forward at the pace of hardware.

records.qualification: The essay states that it shares the expectation of "huge and sudden changes" from technology; it disputes machine autonomy, not technological change. Lanier calls the view he answers "cybernetic totalism"; that is his term, not the pack's.

evidence.passage: That qualitative as well as quantitative aspects of information systems will be accelerated by Moore's Law.
evidence.note: The heading states, in Lanier's wording, one of the beliefs the essay lists in order to dispute them; his answer follows in the same section.

openQuestions.question: Should a relay record (Williams and Srnicek's report of Land's view) be eligible for earliest-located on W01 or W06?
openQuestions.recommended: No; give W01 earliest-located to Sutton 2013 within this group, leave W06 to the Land group's own texts, and keep the relay records as articulations with register relay.

openQuestions.question: Andreessen's 'Patron Saints' list is introduced as 'In lieu of detailed endnotes and citations, read the work of these people'. Is that crediting (explicitly_credits) or naming (cites)?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep cites: the passage recommends reading the people listed but does not state that the manifesto's ideas derive from any one of them.

openQuestions.question: The 2022 Notes and the e/acc repost call capitalism or technocapital an intelligence without the word 'artificial' or 'machine'. Is W06 met?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep as bears_on; the criterion requires an artificial or machine intelligence.

openQuestions.question: The 2022 Notes and the 2026 bayeslord post share a Substack handle (bayeslord, byline 'bayes'); Verdon is identified with @BasedBeffJezos only by the podcast host. Should the integrator join these authors to persons?
openQuestions.recommended: Record authors as printed; join to persons only where the texts themselves state the identity, and attribute the identification to its source.

openQuestions.question: Faggella's essay was read as updated in 2026; the 2023 wording could not be read. Should its records stay dated 2023-11-24?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the posting date with attested 2026-10-15, and ask the cross-family checker to compare the 2024 capture.

openQuestions.question: The AGI 2008 paper PDF states no date; the year rests on the host path agi-conf.org/2008/ and Pavlacka's citation.
openQuestions.recommended: Cross-family checker to confirm the year from the AGI-08 proceedings (IOS Press, Frontiers in AI and Applications 171) or the conference page.

openQuestions.question: Goertzel's profile of de Garis is dated only by Word document properties (2001-05-25).
openQuestions.recommended: Check an archive capture of goertzel.org/benzine/deGaris.htm for the earliest date; keep 2001-05 as a file date otherwise.

openQuestions.question: The Artilect War PDF (created 2014) may differ from the 2005 ETC printing.
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the attested date 2014-03-17; compare one or two quoted passages against a library copy of the 2005 printing if available.

openQuestions.question: The 1990 'Moral Dilemmas' text is read from a 1999 print of the author's page, not the Revue Internationale de Philosophie printing.
openQuestions.recommended: Cross-family checker to open the Wayback capture of the ATR page (2000-10-20) and, if possible, the 1990 journal issue.

openQuestions.question: Hazard notes are set on the 2005 book, the 2008 paper and the 2015 chapter because their forecast-war sections (including predicted assassinations and purges) were excluded from quotation; none of the recorded passages advocates violence.
openQuestions.recommended: Integrator to confirm that the hazard note is wanted for excluded graphic forecast detail as well as for advocacy.

openQuestions.question: Several texts here (Kurzweil 2001, Hanson 1994, Bostrom 2004) are read in later copies; under the attested-date rule they lose earliest-located to 2003 and 2015 texts within this group. Should the integrator compare the 2001-2004 captures before reconciling?
openQuestions.recommended: Ask the cross-family checker to open the listed captures; if the quoted passages match, record the capture dates as attested dates and move earliest-located accordingly (Hanson 1994 for W03; Kurzweil 2001 for W05, W09, W10).

openQuestions.question: The 2015 Edge responses (Rees, Tipler, Pinker, Dennett) are short; should the 10% quotation limit be applied to the response text alone (as here) or to the page?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the response-only counts recorded in documentWords; they are the stricter reading.

openQuestions.question: Torres's article (Truthdig) is an opinion essay in a magazine. Is it admissible as a primary text of its author's argument rather than a press report?
openQuestions.recommended: Admit it as the author's own argument (it states and defends a position under the author's byline), with the relay passage labelled; it is not used as evidence of what Verdon said.

openQuestions.question: The scope's Period bound lists Vinge among the dataset's earlier texts that are "named where they precede a pack headline. Not re-recorded." The brief allows a dataset document to be recorded on a W proposition with existingEntity: true. This draft records Vinge 1993 (dataset source source-vinge-1993-ntrs) as an articulation on W01, where the dataset holds no Vinge 1993 claim on the overlap concept E02. Should the record stay?
openQuestions.recommended: Integrator to decide together with the Moravec 1979 question. Either keep the record and amend the scope's Period bound to say that the dataset's earlier texts are not re-recorded on concepts the dataset already holds, or drop the record and name Vinge 1993 in the W01 searchLog earliestNote as a dataset text that sits beside W01.

openQuestions.question: Hyperstition posts signed 'Old Nick' (2006–2008) include 'Sense and Singularity' (17 July 2007: 'Rigorously conceived Singularity is Intelligence Catastrophe … aka Planetary Meltdown, the Immanent Limit of Capitalism') and 'Yudkowsky' (11 June 2007, quoting 'Staring into the Singularity'). Can they be recorded as Land's?
openQuestions.recommended: Only if a source by Land or a publisher attributes them to him. The Miserablism post is recorded under its signature, with the Fanged Noumena chapter title noted; the others are left out.

openQuestions.question: Should 'Meltdown' be dated by the CCRU's 'Winter, 1997' date for Abstract Culture swarm 1, with the wording attested only from retrieval?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep the 1997 work date with the attested note; ask the cross-family checker to open the 2004 capture, and correct if Fanged Noumena's list of sources (not read) gives another date.

openQuestions.question: Hazard note on 'Meltdown': the text contains second-person fiction of killing 'Turing cops' and the line that 'All political institutions are cyberian military targets'. Is the hazard note warranted?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it as a precaution; nothing from those passages is quoted.

openQuestions.question: Register of 'Meltdown': the W06 passage is framed 'The story goes like this', and other sections of the text are second-person fiction. Should the whole text carry one register?
openQuestions.recommended: All four Meltdown records (W01, W06, W08, W09) are labelled nonfiction: the quoted passages are expository or a narrative framing of a compressed history. The second-person fiction sections are noted in the W06 qualification and not quoted.

openQuestions.question: Circuitries evidence is paraphrase from page images. Should an OCR of the journal's scan be added to the cache so that quotations can be checked mechanically?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, if an OCR tool becomes available; then replace the paraphrases with short quotations (the p. 219 passage on 'a few decades' especially).

openQuestions.question: Mackay and Avanessian's #Accelerate introduction (2014) may also be recorded by the accelerationist-texts group.
openQuestions.recommended: The integrator should keep one document id for it across groups.

openQuestions.question: The scope sets the period at 1985-2026 and says the dataset's earlier texts (including Moravec 1979) are named where they precede a headline and are not re-recorded, while the task brief allows Moravec 1979 and 1989 to be recorded on W propositions with existingEntity: true. After integration the pack records the 1979 essay as an articulation (not earliest located) on W01, W02, W03, W09 and W10 and as context on W08, Moravec 1989 "Genetic Takeover" on W01, W02 and W09, and (further-texts group) Vinge 1993 on W01; by attested date, earliest located goes to de Garis 1989 on W01, W03 and W10, to Minsky 1994 on W02 and, with de Garis 1989 recorded on W09 as context, to Moravec 1989 "Genetic Takeover" on W09.
openQuestions.recommended: Maintainer to decide: amend scope.md (the Period sentence "Not re-recorded" and the Hans Moravec bullet) to allow these dataset texts on W propositions that do not overlap their dataset concepts, or demote the records to named predecessors in the search log.

openQuestions.question: Under the policy the attested date decides the earliest located text. The 1979 and 1988/89 texts are attested from 2001 (byte-identical captures, dataset); several author-hosted texts dated 1989-1993 have captures from 1999-2000 that could not be compared here. If the checker finds them identical, After Life (capture 1999-11-10), The Universal Robot (1999-02-09) and Pigs in Cyberspace (1999-04-27) would be attested earlier than the 1979 essay.
openQuestions.recommended: Ask the cross-family checker to compare the listed captures; then decide whether the attested-date rule should apply to author-hosted copies of texts whose own date is far earlier, and adjust earliest-located roles.

openQuestions.question: Several Moravec texts are adapted from Mind Children (1988), which was not read; repeated wording (the brain-replacement scenario, the "mind children ... bow out" passage) recurs across 1979, 1989, 1991, the Robot preview and 2000.
openQuestions.recommended: Keep one record per text as drafted; if a legal copy of Mind Children becomes available, add it and re-check earliest-located roles.
